reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 34. Nay or No: 6. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 39 (98%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

finance.disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
finance.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.
finance.scope_note: Figures are committee receipts and itemized Schedule A for this two-year cycle only. This is not career fundraising. Schedule E outside spending is not included.
finance.contributor_note: Itemized Schedule A receipts for this principal campaign committee and cycle, grouped by contributor name. Memo lines are omitted so an earmark is not counted twice. Unitemized donations are not in this list. Not every Schedule A row was retrieved, so this ranking uses the largest receipts returned and can miss contributors whose gifts are smaller but add up.

pacs.donors_note: Disclosed donors to this committee were not retrieved for this cycle.

finance.pac_note: Committees and party committees among the itemized contributors, largest amounts first. Up to five. Their donors are Schedule A filings of that committee for the same cycle, disclosed donors only.

lobbying_summary.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.

running.label: Candidates who filed with the FEC for this seat. Filing is not the same as being on the ballot. Primary results and ballot access are not shown.
incumbent_notes: Michael Lawler has a 2026 filing for this seat (FEC H2NY17162, FEC lists: Incumbent). Not counted below.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

party_line.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

Today, I welcomed Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to the Hudson Valley to discuss the Constitution Pipeline and the need to lower energy costs for New Yorkers.

During the visit to Cricket Valley Energy, we highlighted the Trump administration’s $42 million investment to advance the proposed 125-mile natural gas pipeline from Pennsylvania to New York, which will expand access to reliable energy and help lower electricity and home heating costs across the Northeast.

I’ll continue working to advance critical energy infrastructure, strengthen reliability, and make energy more affordable for Hudson Valley families and businesses.

From helping lead the town’s Memorial Day parades to his instrumental role in establishing the veterans memorials at Routes 9W and 210, Donald worked to ensure that our nation’s heroes would always be remembered.

His presence at community gatherings and veterans ceremonies will be deeply missed, but his legacy will live on through the many lives he touched. Rest in peace, Cool Breeze. Thank you for your service and your unwavering commitment to our veterans and community.

Americans deserve transparency and accountability in our elections. That means having clear rules to prevent candidates from using campaign coordination arrangements to get around finance limits.

Right now, coordination between political campaigns and super PACs can allow candidates to circumvent contribution limits and benefit from unlimited spending. 

The Stop Illegal Super PAC Coordination Act would help close these loopholes, strengthen campaign finance rules, and protect the integrity of our elections.

It was especially meaningful to join the Melanie Chianese Foundation, survivors, advocates, community organizations, and law enforcement in the Town of Wappinger for a special Community Day for Domestic Violence Awareness to support victims of domestic violence and their families.

Cheryl’s tireless advocacy helped make Melanie’s Law a reality in New York, expanding protections for vulnerable family and household members. I’m proud to support bringing those same protections to families nationwide through federal legislation.

matches.bill_title: Stop Illegal Super PAC Coordination Act
matches.matched_text: stop illegal super pac coordination act

post.text:
Americans deserve transparency and accountability in our elections. That means having clear rules to prevent candidates from using campaign coordination arrangements to get around finance limits.

Right now, coordination between political campaigns and super PACs can allow candidates to circumvent contribution limits and benefit from unlimited spending. 

The Stop Illegal Super PAC Coordination Act would help close these loopholes, strengthen campaign finance rules, and protect the integrity of our elections.
